subject: Request: Phased commitment + billing credit addendum for Order SF-8421
messages:
From: Ravi Menon <ravi.menon@skyforge.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: SkyForge Procurement <procurement@skyforge.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: Phased commitment + billing credit addendum for Order SF-8421

Hi Stephanie / Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We reviewed the order internally and have one operational ask before procurement can route this to legal: SkyForge needs the committed GPU capacity to be staged across three quarterly phases instead of the single upfront commitment in the Order Form. The reasons are resource planning and a phased internal launch.

Concretely:
- Phase 1 (Q3): 25% of committed V100-equivalent throughput
- Phase 2 (Q4): 50% cumulative
- Phase 3 (Q1 next year): 100% cumulative

Because of the slower ramp, we also need a short billing mitigation: a one-time consumption credit that offsets the difference in month 1 billing while we ramp. Would Redwood be able to accommodate a credit applied to the first invoice tied to milestone delivery?

If you prefer, we can accept an addendum to the MSA + an adjusted Order Form (we can do a single addendum that amends both). Attaching a high-level rollout schedule for context.

Ravi
Ravi Menon
Head of Cloud Ops, SkyForge AI
ravi.menon@skyforge.ai

Attachment: orderform_phased_schedule.xlsx (spreadsheet - phased capacity proposal)

Subject: Re: Request: Phased commitment + billing credit addendum for Order SF-8421

Hi Ravi — thanks for the clarity and the schedule. We can support a phased commitment, and a single addendum that amends the Order Form + MSA makes sense operationally.

Next steps I propose:
1) Internal redline draft from Redwood to capture the phased delivery schedule and the one-time billing credit (T&Cs for credit application).
2) Karthik to confirm the commercial credit band we can offer while preserving the committed economics.
3) Laura to review the MSA language and suggest guardrails (e.g., milestone acceptance, rollback if capacity unavailable).
4) We circulate a single clean addendum and run via DocuSign once legal/procurement sign off.

I'm attaching our proposed addendum redline that maps to MSA sections 2.1 (Commitment), 4.3 (Billing) and Exhibit A. It's a working draft — Laura, commenting welcome.

Best,
Stephanie
Senior Account Lead | Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2026 14:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Phased commitment + billing credit addendum for Order SF-8421

Ravi / team — we can do a one-time invoice credit. Suggested commercial approach: credit equal to the delta between billed minimum in month 1 under original order vs billed consumption given phased capacity, capped at $25k (one-time). That keeps the math simple for both sides.

Couple of asks from my side:
- Can you confirm the trigger milestone for Phase 2 (development completion or production traffic > X)? We should tie phase triggers to objective events.
- Do you need the credit applied as a line-item credit or as a prepaid top-up reversal?

Marissa — can you pre-approve the credit cap range so we can put numbers in the addendum?

Karthik
Director, Sales | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Request: Phased commitment + billing credit addendum for Order SF-8421

Thanks for the draft, Stephanie. Quick legal read: the overall approach is fine but we should tighten a few points to avoid open-ended obligations. Proposed edits (high level):
- Replace subjective "milestone delivery" language with defined triggers in Exhibit A (we need dates or measurable criteria).
- Limit Redwood's obligation to deliver phased capacity to compatibility with the model variant and hardware availability; add a fallback clause that permits substitution with equivalent performance profiles and a notice window.
- For the credit: specify it as a one-time invoice credit, applied to Invoice #1 after Phase 1 acceptance; cap language should include a numeric ceiling and a process for disputes.
- Add a short audit clause so SkyForge can request usage and allocation logs for the first 90 days post-rollout (reasonable, limited scope).

I've annotated SF-8421_proposed_addendum_redline.docx and attached a redline that updates MSA sections 2.1 and 4.3 and adds an Exhibit A template (MSA_v3_section_refs.pdf contains the section map). If you all are good with the commercial cap, I'll convert to a clean addendum for signature.

Laura Bennett
Associate General Counsel | Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com

All — this looks good. We agree to the proposed approach and the credit cap of $25k is acceptable. Two small asks before signature:
1) Can Redwood add a short clause allowing an earlier acceleration to Phase 2 if our traffic exceeds the Phase 1 forecast (we'd trigger and pay the delta)?
2) Please include the timeline table in Exhibit A as the definitive schedule so procurement can route the addendum quickly.

If you send the clean addendum I can run a final procurement pass and sign via DocuSign. Thanks for moving quickly.

Ravi
